statement: Aurora PLM stays as the engineering design system and must be integrated with SAP for the bill of materials and changes, not replaced.
Engineering changes after release are emailed to planning and the old parts list stays in use, so the shop builds to outdated revisions.
The manufacturing bill of materials and routings are built by hand in Excel and on printed sheets, and parts are missing from the export.
Material requirements are netted by hand and stock reserved for one project is used for another, so projects stop for missing parts.
Material shortages that stop production must be cut by half through automatic requirements planning per project.
Supplier delivery dates sit in the buyer's own spreadsheet and the production schedule is not updated when castings or drives are late.
Purchases above £20,000 must be approved by the Operations Director in the system.
Capacity per work centre is checked by experience, and urgent jobs are slotted in without updating the schedule.
Inspection results and non-conformances are on paper and certificates are written in Word, with no link to the project cost.
Project costs are allocated by hand and margin is known only after delivery, with work in progress estimated quarterly.
Project cost variance must stay under 5% against budget with margin visible during the project.
Staged invoices are raised by hand from the contract, so milestones are billed late and scope extras are missed.
On-time delivery must reach at least 92%, up from 71%.
